payload.name: Enumerate career-best achievements with superlative synonym searches
payload.description: When a question asks which career-high, personal-best, record, or highest-ever performances someone had, search each metric category and expand with superlative synonyms before answering.
content: When a question asks which career-high, personal-best, record, or 'highest ever' performances/achievements someone had, treat it as an enumeration: the answer may span multiple distinct metric categories (e.g., points, assists, sales, grades), each stored in a separate memory.

After the first retrieval, do not stop at the first memory that literally contains 'career-high' or 'record'. Run additional searches using superlative synonyms (highest, best, most, top, personal best, all-time) combined with likely metric/domain nouns relevant to the person's activity.

Before finalizing, check whether retrieved evidence covers every plausible metric category in the question; if additional metrics or domains remain unsearched, continue searching until no new superlative achievement appears.

solves: Diagnosed cause: 'which career-high performances' was treated as single-slot; only the memory with literal 'career-high' was used and a different category phrased 'highest ever score' was missed. Because record achievements use varied metric wording, enumerate each category with superlative synonyms and check sufficiency before answering. Applies to list-of-records questions; not single-stat recall.
